newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-FRYDEK'S TRANSFER CLOUDED IN CONFUSION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRYDEK'S TRANSFER CLOUDED IN CONFUSION.

text.p: Sparta Prague midfielder Martin Frydek's transfer to Germany's Bayern Leverkusen was clouded in confusion on Tuesday when Sparta officials denied the move had been finalised.
Last week the two teams appeared to reach an agreement.

But Czech international Frydek said on Tuesday that the chances of his moving to the German club had dimmed greatly after Sparta's Slovak-led management team said two signatures of board members were needed for the transfer to be approved.

"I am very upset, I don't know what conditions complicated the situation, maybe financial ones. Right now, I see my chances at leaving for Leverkusen at about 50-50," Frydek was quoted as saying in the daily Sport.
Frydek's agent Zdenek Nehoda said he was shown a signed contract between Bayern Leverkusen and Sparta, signed by its general manager Gejza Sestak and his German counterpart.
Sparta President Milan Valasik, however, told Sport that under a club directive two board members must sign agreements concerning player transfers.
"Sestak, of course, has the right to sign but his signature alone is not enough," Valasik said.
"My personal opinion is that the amount Leverkusen is offering is inadequate."
